status: 겨울철새, 해마다 수천 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록

months.note: 11월 초순에 와서 3월 하순까지 머물며, 5월 중순까지 남은 기록도 있다.

summary: 11월 초순에 와서 3월 하순까지 머무는 흔한 겨울철새로, 해안에서 떨어진 먼바다에 많고 연안이나 강 하류에서는 드물게 보인다. 혼자 또는 작은 무리로 잠수해 물고기를 잡는다. 회색머리아비보다 월동하는 수가 많지만, 다른 아비류처럼 어선에서 버린 폐기름에 오염되거나 어망에 걸려 질식하는 등 여러 까닭으로 수가 줄고 있는 것으로 추정된다. 유라시아 북부와 알래스카 서북부에서 번식하고 겨울에는 남쪽으로 옮겨 가 지낸다.

art.subject: Black-throated Loon (Gavia arctica), adult in winter (non-breeding) plumage, as seen off Korean coasts from November to March: crown and hindneck dark slate-grey, the dark cap reaching down to the eye; chin, throat and foreneck clean white with no dark line across the throat, separated from the dark hindneck by a sharp straight border; back and wings plain blackish-grey; underparts white, with a broad white patch on the rear flanks rising above the waterline towards the back. Straight, pointed dagger-shaped bill, grey with a dark tip and ridge; red eye; legs black.
art.pose: swimming low on the open sea, about to dive
art.scene: open sea off the Korean coast in winter with a grey swell; no people, buildings or text
views: adult winter, side view swimming: dark slate-grey cap and hindneck, clean white throat and foreneck with a sharp border, plain blackish back, broad white rear-flank patch rising above the waterline, straight pointed bill
adult winter, head and neck detail in side view: white throat without any thin dark cross-line, sharp straight border between dark hindneck and white foreneck, dagger bill, red eye
art.build: Large loon, 72–78cm, much bigger than a Mallard and noticeably larger and heavier than Red-throated Loon; long, low body, thick neck and rounded head. Bill straight and pointed, dagger-like, shorter than the head, held level. Legs set far back near the tail. Swims low in the water and dives for fish; often only the back, neck and head show. In flight long-bodied, the feet projecting beyond the tail.
avoid: Do not paint a thin dark strap across the throat or leave out the white rear-flank patch; those mark Pacific Loon (Gavia pacifica).
Do not paint a slim upturned bill or a white-speckled back; that is Red-throated Loon (Gavia stellata).
Do not paint an ivory-yellow bill; that is Yellow-billed Loon (Gavia adamsii).
